# Lost distinctions, introduced commitments, vanished uncertainty, broken dependencies, blocked criticism

I'll compare the frozen corpus prose, the actual expression (a Lean file + a non-Lean semantic class description + an application of it to the frozen prose), the independent reading supplied, and the proposed language. I do not install repairs.

## 0. What the "selected carrier" is, and why that matters here

The chosen carrier is the frozen **non-Lean semantic class** (RSS), not the Lean file. That choice has an immediate consequence: any distinction the Lean file makes *mechanically* that RSS makes only by *stipulation in prose* is a real difference, and any commitment the Lean file refuses to make that RSS permits is likewise a real difference. The Lean file declares upfront:

> "The language does not assert which conjectures are true; it provides the vocabulary to state them and to record refutations as proofs of negation or as explicit counterexamples."
> "Expiry deletes the record … This is stated as a possible disagreement, not resolved."
> "Source assumptions are not primitive. … This is an expressive limitation."
> "Replication is not primitive. … This is an expressive limitation."

RSS, by contrast, *makes* expiry, release, ties, replica-relative time, provenance, and resource models into named primitives and reading-parameters. So the two carriers are not aligned: one treats several source disagreements as *unresolved* and says so as a limitation; the other treats them as *expressible* and says so as a permit. The actual expression chooses RSS, so the frozen corpus's hedges get re-encoded through a vocabulary that has more slots than the Lean file's vocabulary has. That is the terrain where the specific defects below live.

## 1. Lost distinctions

**(a) "Duplicate deliveries" vs. "near-duplicate deliveries" — a distinction the source does not draw, which RSS draws as a primitive split.**

The frozen prose says:

> "Duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority."

The Lean file's `exact_duplicate` matches this faithfully, and its note reads:

> "'Duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority' is represented by `exact_duplicate`: two records with all five fields equal are inert with respect to each other. The language does not say that near-duplicates are inert; they may be alternatives."

RSS then introduces a *named* distinction the source never has:

> "**Exact duplication**: … **Near-duplication**: two deliveries share booking and revision but differ in kind, quantity, or expiry."

The actual expression repeats it:

> "Near-duplicates—same booking and revision, differing in kind or quantity or expiry—are not covered by this statement and remain candidates for conflict."

The lost distinction is between *the source's own ambiguity about near-duplicates* (the source says "duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority" and does not explicitly consider whether near-duplicates are "duplicates" for this purpose) and *a primitive category in RSS*. The source's "duplicate deliveries" is a phrase whose scope is genuinely unclear; RSS turns the unclear scope into a two-term partition ("exact" / "near"), each with a defined behavior. That is not a misreading of a sentence so much as a *promotion of an ambiguity into a taxonomy*. The Lean file preserves the ambiguity more honestly: it defines `exact_duplicate` and then explicitly declines to say what happens to near-duplicates ("they may be alternatives" — a conjecture). RSS decides — by naming a category — that whatever shares booking and revision but differs in a field is a "near-duplicate," full stop.

Distinguishing case: the source also entertains (via "different bookings need not share the same choice") the possibility that two records with *the same booking and same revision* but *different kinds* are "different records tied at a greatest revision." The Lean file encodes that as `alternatives_at_greatest` with `¬ exact_duplicate`. RSS encodes it as near-duplication. Both are expressible; only the Lean file states the tie/supersession residual as a *consequence*, whereas RSS asserts it as a category. The lost distinction is that "not exactly identical" is not a positive category in the source, but RSS makes it one.

**(b) The source's "tilt" is hedged, but RSS's "reading" is a positive choice-token, not a hedge.**

Frozen prose:

> "The snapshot description tilts toward the first: a higher revision supersedes lower revisions, and expiry can make a hold reserve zero. It does not say expiry removes the supersession. So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture…"

The expression carries this as:

> "The source's own phrase 'the snapshot description tilts toward the first' is carried as the source's own hedge, not upgraded to a commitment, and RSS preserves that hedge by treating the tilt as a reading preference rather than a fact."

The distinction lost is between **(i)** a *reasoner's tilt* — an epistemic preference about which of two conjectures is better supported by the text — and **(ii)** a *reading* — a policy RSS treats as one of two equally available options. The source's "tilt" is an indication about *probative weight*; RSS's "reading" is a *parametric slot*. Treating the tilt as a reading preference converts a claim about evidence into a claim about an option list. The prose-escape even registers this as an interpretive choice ("could be contested"), but the *distinction* — tilt vs. reading-option — is not preserved as a distinction; it's collapsed into one kind of thing, "reading."

**(c) Global availability "not even convex"**

Frozen prose:

> "If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one."

The Lean file *cannot* express non-convexity of a set of possible global availability values, because it only computes lower and upper bounds over `Nat`-derived `Int`s, per booking. That is a real expressive limit (the Lean file itself does not flag this one explicitly). RSS, however, could have preserved the non-convexity distinction. It doesn't; it converts it to:

> "availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one. … RSS represents both as readings."

But "RSS represents both as readings" does not preserve *non-convexity* — it preserves *two bounds* (a pessimistic and an optimistic reading). The distinction between "an interval with possible gaps" and "an interval" vanishes: the expression announces "possibly not even a convex one" in the voice of the source, then reduces to min/max readings. The substantive claim "possibly not even convex" is stated and then not carried into RSS's vocabulary; RSS offers only "lower bound" and "upper bound" readings, which are convex by construction.

## 2. Introduced commitments

**(a) A commitment to a first-person voice that RSS's own vocabulary contradicts.**

The expression opens:

> "The warehouse snapshot is a collection of rival stories. **I will not compute one answer for it.** I will say what it is, what can be said about it in the vocabulary of stories, viewpoints, readings, and accounts, and where that vocabulary runs out."

Its own independent reader flags this:

> "The expression begins with a first-person declaration ('I will not compute one answer') that sits uneasily with RSS's own framing, which is about accounts, not voices. If the 'I' is an account, it is not named; if it is the semantics speaking, the semantics has no first person."

This is a *reader-visible* introduced commitment: a stance the source does not take and RSS does not license. RSS's primitives have "account" and "viewpoint," not "I." The source's own voice is third-person and about people ("People may disagree about whether uncertainty should be retained"). The "I" imports an agent that neither the source nor RSS names. It is small, but it is a commitment not derivable from the carrier.

**(b) A commitment that the set-of-reservations is "more informative than the sign" — promoted from source conjecture to RSS assertion.**

Source:

> "A conjecture: the sign of availability is less important than the set of reservations that produce it…"

Note: *conjecture*. The expression writes:

> "RSS: availability is a derived quantity that can be negative under a reading; the sign is a signal, not an error; the set of reservations is more informative than the sign. The conjecture that the sign of availability is less important than the set of reservations that produce it—RSS accepts this as a conjecture about a projection."

Two competing framings appear in adjacent sentences: (i) RSS *states as its own* "the set of reservations is more informative than the sign," and (ii) the source's conjecture is "accepted as a conjecture about a projection." The reader of the expression receives both the promotion ("RSS: … more informative than the sign") and the demotion ("accepted as a conjecture"). If RSS's own statement is not a conjecture, then the source's conjecture has been upgraded to a semantic-class assertion; if it is a conjecture, then the "RSS:" prefix is misusing the semantics class name. The reader's independent section notes this same stress:

> "Whether any single-number availability is authorized. The expression says a projection is 'a loss of information'… Whether that is a defect or a feature is left to accounts."

**(c) A commitment that "criticisms and refutations are local to accounts and do not force global agreement" is fit for the source.**

The source's third disagreement asks what a criticism *targets*; it does not commit to any locality thesis about criticisms. RSS asserts:

> "Refutations are local to accounts and do not force global agreement."

The expression repeats this and then applies it. But the frozen source contains, verbatim:

> "False or incomplete proposals are not discarded; they are part of the evidence about how people understand the system."

That is a claim about *retention*, not locality. The expression silently substitutes an *account-locality thesis* for the source's *retention*-thesis. Whether refutations are account-local is a substantive philosophical commitment about disagreement; the source does not make it, and the expression does, without flagging it as added.

**(d) A commitment that RSS is the correct carrier for the source — though the packet already fixed that choice.**

The reader's section "Against the non-Lean stance" says:

> "non-Lean semantics is not automatically freer than a Lean translation; it is differently constrained. It cannot state a theorem, cannot check a proof, and cannot mechanically distinguish a refutation from a contradiction-in-prose."

The expression never argues for the choice; it simply performs it. Whether that is a "commitment" or a "context" is arguable (the packet selects the carrier), but the *consequences* of the choice — e.g., refutation becomes one of three prose-defined moves, none mechanically checkable — are not registered by the expression. RSS's own description of refutation is where this becomes visible:

> "A refutation is one of: (a) a counterexample within an account's own viewpoint; (b) a derivation of inconsistency within an account's own reading; or (c) a demonstration that a conjecture depends on an assumption that another account rejects."

Compare the Lean file, which is more modest: a refutation is a snapshot together with `¬ c snap`. RSS's (b) and (c) have no mechanical analogue; they are refutation-shaped speech acts. The expression adopts RSS's wider sense without noting the loss of the Lean sense.

## 3. Vanished uncertainty

**(a) The source's "possibly not even a convex one"** — stated, then dropped (see 1(c)). The uncertainty about *shape* of the availability set vanishes into a min/max story.

**(b) The source's worry about "physics of possibility smuggling."**

Source:

> "A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain."

The expression converts this into:

> "The criticism that once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain—RSS accepts this criticism as a criticism of a specific projection, not of the semantics itself."

The uncertainty in the original is about whether the *move to possible worlds* was legitimate in the first place. The expression reclassifies the criticism as targeting a *projection* — i.e., it localizes a criticism that was, in the source, potentially global. That is a substantive downgrade of the criticism (see also §5).

**(c) Source's ambiguity about whether the snapshot is "the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica's view."** The expression's reader's view flags:

> "Whether the bag is union, intersection, or single-replica view. The expression says RSS 'does not decide,' and that this is represented as a viewpoint-relative matter. But it also says the snapshot is 'described as replicated,' without deciding which replication semantics the frozen source actually intends."

The uncertainty is *named* but not *carried as an open question in RSS's vocabulary*. RSS has no primitive for "the source's replication intent is unresolved." "Viewpoint" is defined as (coordinate, bag) — but the bag is just a bag. The uncertainty about what *kind* of bag it is has nowhere to live except in a prose comment. It is named, not encoded.

**(d) The `prose-escape` says "no Lean fragment is being obstructed" — but this is itself a commitment, not an uncertainty.** The reader notes:

> "The prose-escape block's claim that no Lean fragment is being obstructed cannot be verified from the expression alone, and it should not be treated as a proof that the source contained no Lean — only as a commitment of the expression not to represent one."

This is a vanished uncertainty: the expression converts an *unverifiable-hence-open* question ("did the source contain Lean fragments?") into an *asserted absence* ("no Lean fragment is being obstructed"). The Lean file's presence in the packet certainly means the packet contained a Lean expression, even if *that* Lean expression was a proposed language rather than a translation of a fragment. Whether the frozen source *contains* Lean is a separate question from whether the *translation attempt* is obstructing one.

## 4. Broken dependencies

**(a) The relation between `ReservationRule` and `possible_reservations` is broken by declaration order in the Lean file.**

In the Lean file:

```
def rules_disagree (r1 r2 : ReservationRule) (snap : Snapshot) : Prop :=
  ∃ b, possible_reservations_with r1 snap b ≠ possible_reservations_with r2 snap b

/-- Reservation possibilities parameterized by a rule. -/
def possible_reservations_with (rule : ReservationRule) (snap : Snapshot) (b : Booking) : List Quantity :=
  ...
```

`rules_disagree` references `possible_reservations_with` before the latter is declared. In Lean 4, this order would produce an "unknown constant" error unless forward declaration or reordering is used. This is a defect *in the Lean file*, which is part of the frozen corpus but not the selected carrier. It is still worth recording: the *source*'s dependency ("two rules disagree on a snapshot iff their possible-reservation lists differ for some booking") is broken at the level of the file. However, since the selected carrier is the non-Lean RSS, this defect is *not* the fault of the selected language; it is a translator/compiler-bridge defect in the packet. Recording a repair without installing it: reorder the two `def`s, or declare `possible_reservations_with` first.

**(b) RSS declares `provenance` a field of a story, but does not make it a field of a delivery.**

RSS's Primitives say:

> "A story has a booking, a revision, a kind (hold or release), a quantity, an expiry, and a **provenance** (which delivery or set of deliveries it is drawn from)."
> "A **Bag**: an unordered collection of deliveries."

But a *delivery* is defined only as "an event that makes a record available." A record's fields are booking, revision, kind, quantity, expiry. So provenance has no field-content to be drawn from — it can only point to a delivery, which is an event, not a record. Then:

> "**Exact duplication**: two deliveries are exact duplicates if all record fields and provenance are equal."

But provenance is defined as "which delivery or set of deliveries [the story] is drawn from" — that is, provenance is a property of a *story*, not a *delivery*. The definition of exact duplication therefore refers to a property that deliveries do not have. This is a broken dependency: the primitive "delivery" lacks the field that "exact duplication" quantifies over, and which "story" has.

The expression compounds this: it says

> "RSS: exact duplicates are inert in all readings. Near-duplicates—same booking and revision, differing in kind or quantity or expiry—are not covered by this statement…"

No mention of provenance in this restatement. So the very field that RSS made a primitive to distinguish "exact" from "near" disappears when the distinction is applied. The reader's section catches this obliquely:

> "**That 'authority' is the right word for what exact duplicates fail to add.** 'Authority does not accumulate by repetition' is a gloss on 'duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority,' but the meaning of 'authority' in the source is not defined in the expression."

**(c) "Computing the availability" — RSS's own primitives force a computation route that its own noncomputability refuses.**

RSS says:

> "Availability is a derived quantity that can be negative under a reading … the set of reservations is more informative than the sign."

But deriving availability requires *summing reservations*, which requires *selecting* a reservation per booking, which requires *a reading*. RSS's noncomputability says no reading is selected. So "derived quantity" is a misdescription: under RSS, availability is a *derived-per-reading* quantity. The expression does hedge ("under a reading"), but the phrase "is a derived quantity" does not. The Lean file at least treats availability as a function `Snapshot → List Booking → Int` (an actual derivation), not as a *per-reading* quantity. The RSS substitution breaks a dependency: what was a function of a snapshot in the Lean carrier becomes a function of a viewpoint-and-reading pair in RSS, and no formal slot replaces the old one.

## 5. Blocked criticism

**(a) The criticism about the "possible worlds" smuggled notion is *localized* to a projection.**

Source:

> "A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain."

The criticism as originally stated is *directed at the representational move itself* — arguably against the very idea of representing alternatives as a set of possible reservations. The expression *re-scopes* the criticism to a projection rather than the representation:

> "RSS accepts this criticism as a criticism of a specific projection, not of the semantics itself."

This blocks the criticism at its most potent level: a criticism that RSS's primitive vocabulary — story, viewpoint, alternative compatibility — already traffics in possible-world talk, and hence cannot avoid the smuggled notion, is redirected to "a specific projection" and thereby neutralized by the semantics' own partition (projections are losses; not-privileged). A reader who wants to say "the whole RSS apparatus trades in smuggled possibility" finds the expression has already declined that reading. The source's criticism, read uncharitably to RSS, is blocked.

**(b) The criticism "capacity may be misleading" is localized to the primitive "coordinate."**

Source:

> "A criticism: if availability is allowed to be negative, then capacity is not a hard constraint, and the word 'capacity' may be misleading; it is more like a soft target or a reporting threshold."

Expression:

> "RSS carries this as a criticism of the primitive 'coordinate,' which is a parameter of a viewpoint, not an absolute fact."

The source's criticism is about *a word and a concept in the system description*. The expression re-locates it to *a definitional primitive of RSS*. Whether that move is a faithful carrying-forward is arguable — but it has the effect of making the criticism sound like a complaint about RSS's choice of primitive name rather than a substantive objection to the underlying model. The reader's section names this kind of move:

> "**Against the treatment of negativity.** … The expression concedes this criticism … but treats it as a criticism of the primitive, not of the reconstruction."

**(c) The criticism "any single-number availability is a projection that discards information" is promoted from conjecture to fact about projections, closing off its own contestability.**

Source:

> "A conjecture: any single-number availability is a projection that discards information, and different projections can disagree even when they respect the snapshot."

Expression:

> "The conjecture that any single-number availability is a projection that discards information—RSS states this as a fact about projections, not a conjecture."

The reader flags this:

> "**That 'any single-number availability is a projection that discards information' — RSS states this as a fact about projections, not a conjecture.**"

Once it becomes a definitional fact about projections, the *criticism* — that non-projection might also discard information, or that projections might not always discard the information the source cares about — is blocked from being raised against RSS's own framing. The definitional status immunizes the claim.

**(d) Source's phrase "keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction's only honest form" is *endorsed* rather than held open.**

Source: a reconstructive claim.

Expression: repeats the sentence and frames the *whole non-Lean apparatus* as the representation of this claim ("In RSS, this is represented by inquiry states…"). Reader's section:

> "A critic could say this is a rhetorical move: by calling visibility the only honest form, the expression immunizes itself against demands for resolution."

That is a blocked criticism in the specific sense: the criticism that the expression is *not* honest because it refuses to project is ruled out by the expression's framing of "only honest form." The framing is a rhetorical device that forecloses the criticism before it can be raised.

## 6. Where is the defect? (attribution)

Partly the defects are in the **translator** (the expression) and partly in the **selected language** (RSS), partly in the **compiler bridge** (the Lean file's declaration-order issue), and partly in the **reader's section** (the source-text-withheld reading).

- **Translator (expression)**: the "I" voice; the promotion of RSS-owned statements amidst conjectures; the re-scoping of criticisms to projections and primitives; the elision of non-convexity; the omission of provenance from the exact/near-duplicate restatement.
- **Selected language (RSS)**: the broken dependency of provenance; the missing per-reading availability slot; the absence of a primitive for "source's replication intent is unresolved"; the substitution of an account-locality thesis for a retention-thesis; the reification of "near-duplicate" as a category.
- **Compiler bridge (Lean file)**: the forward-reference bug in `rules_disagree`.
- **Reader**: accurately identifies most of the above but also *itself* suggests that the question "did the source contain Lean fragments?" can be settled by the prose-escape block, then immediately retracts. The reader is careful, but the section "Source quotations visible in the expression" implies the reader has access to the expression's quotations of the source without access to the source — a fact which the reader notes. This is a *reader* problem, not an expression or language problem.

The Lean file's own header explicitly declares its expressive limits: replication, physical resource sharing, provenance, per-replica time. RSS claims to *add* these as primitives. The comparison of the two carriers would be a useful appendix to the packet: the Lean file says what it cannot express; RSS says what it can express but *does not say* — for provenance, for replication intent, for non-convexity — that these primitives are themselves incomplete. "Provenance" without a mechanism for comparing provenances is a word, not a primitive. That is a defect of the *selected language*, and the expression does not repair it.

## 7. Disposition

Unresolved. The principal defects are: the promotion of source-framed conjectures into RSS-owned assertions (§2(b),(c), §5(c)); the localization of criticisms to projections/definitions with a neutralizing effect (§5(a),(b)); the loss of the source's "possibly not even convex" (unrepresentable in Lean, dropped in RSS); the provenance break in RSS (a defect of the selected language, which the expression did not repair); and the Lean carrier's forward-reference bug (a translator/bridge defect). The most substantive prose objections — against smuggling possibility, against the "only honest form" rhetorical immunizations, and against the loss of a mechanically checkable refutation — remain admissible as prose objections even though RSS cannot encode the criticism of itself. A conflicting interpretation is possible: one could argue that RSS's "reading" primitive *is* the way the source's tilted-but-not-settled choice is preserved, and that the expression's classification of the tilt as a reading is an enhancement, not a defect. I record that possibility without choosing it.

messages.content: Respond in ordinary prose, with optional formal expressions or fenced source code. No JSON envelope is required. Preserve uncertainty and any substantive criticism that cannot be expressed in the selected carrier. You are not being asked for a scalar score or a creativity verdict.

Selected carrier: the frozen model-proposed non-Lean semantic class. Use its own meanings and relations without requiring programmability, decidability or a Lean translation. Preserve any unsupported substantive content or criticism in ordinary prose.

Compare the original frozen prose, the actual expression, its independent reading and the proposed language. Find specific lost distinctions, introduced commitments, vanished uncertainty, broken dependencies or blocked criticism where the evidence supports them. Quote the source and expression and give a distinguishing reading or case. Consider whether the defect is in the translator, reader, selected language, compiler bridge or the probe itself. Do not infer impossibility merely because one model failed to express something. A substantive prose objection remains admissible even if the selected formal language cannot encode it. The original conjecture and language remain frozen: record proposed repairs without installing them. An unresolved or competing interpretation is an acceptable disposition.

  "corpus": {
    "corpus_id": "41efaae132de8b176c85b109b39ab39738708355742354d2e9714aeaf87ecb55",
    "model": "deepseek-flash",
    "origin_plan_id": "842e2fc309a1dd76503a7d275460c906571732ac69d513fc15a097998e15d417",
    "problem": "A replicated warehouse reservation snapshot is described by a capacity, logical current time, and an unordered bag of delivered records. Each record names a booking, revision, hold or release, quantity and expiry. Duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority. A higher revision supersedes lower revisions. Different records tied at a greatest revision can remain unresolved alternatives; different bookings need not share the same choice. A release or expired hold can reserve zero while an active hold reserves its quantity. Availability can be negative. People may disagree about whether uncertainty should be retained, what expiry does to obsolete records, what a criticism targets, and which source assumptions an account depends on. Explore this problem in prose. Correctness is not a condition for preserving a conjecture; false or incomplete proposals remain material for inquiry.",
    "schema": "minireason.language-corpus.v1",
    "text": "A replicated warehouse snapshot is not a single ledger but a cloud of rival stories about what has been promised. The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates, but the records arrive as a bag: orderless, possibly repeated, possibly stale, possibly contradictory. The first useful conjecture is that the snapshot's job is not to compute one timeless answer but to decide which conflicts are still alive. Duplicate delivery of the same booking, revision, kind, quantity, and expiry adds nothing; authority does not accumulate by repetition. A higher revision kills lower revisions for that booking, but only within the booking. Two bookings can disagree about which revision they have accepted without infecting each other.

For any one booking, the natural reconstruction is to group its records by revision, then keep only the greatest revision present. Within that greatest revision, a hold and a release cannot both be in force as the same fact; they are alternatives. An expired hold and a release both reserve zero. An active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives, not a sum and not a vote. That is a deliberate refusal: the rules do not say how to merge them, so the snapshot should retain the possibility that any one is the true one, or that none is, depending on what "true" is taken to mean.

Availability is then capacity minus whatever reservation is actually selected, but the word "actually" hides the problem. If each booking's greatest revision is unambiguous, availability may still be negative if the selected holds exceed capacity. Negative availability is not an error in the arithmetic; it is a signal that the warehouse has over-promised relative to this reconstruction. If different bookings have unresolved alternatives, availability is not a number but a set or an interval, and possibly not even a convex one. A pessimistic reading takes the maximum hold among alternatives for each booking; an optimistic reading takes the minimum. Neither is forced by the snapshot alone.

Now the disagreements begin.

One disagreement is whether uncertainty should be retained at all. A reconciler might collapse each tie to the largest quantity, or to the earliest expiry, or to the record with some lexical tiebreak, and thereby produce a single availability number. That is convenient, but it manufactures authority. Another reconciler might keep all alternatives and report a range. That preserves honesty but makes downstream decisions harder. The snapshot description does not settle which is correct; it only says tied records can remain unresolved. A conjecture: the more useful representation is a partial order of possible reservations, not a set, because some alternatives may be compatible with others across bookings while others are not. A criticism: once you move to a set of possible worlds, you have smuggled in a notion of possibility that the original bag did not contain.

A second disagreement concerns expiry and obsolete records. If logical current time is past a hold's expiry, that hold reserves zero. But does expiry erase the record, demote it, or merely change its effect? Suppose a booking has revision 5 expired and revision 3 active. Higher revision supersedes lower revision, so revision 5 wins, and because it is expired it reserves zero. Revision 3 is obsolete and should not be resurrected. That reading treats revision as authority and expiry as effect. Another reading treats expiry as deleting the record from the bag, after which revision 3 becomes greatest and active, so the booking reserves again. These give opposite answers. The snapshot description tilts toward the first: a higher revision supersedes lower revisions, and expiry can make a hold reserve zero. It does not say expiry removes the supersession. So the first is better supported, but the second remains a live conjecture, especially if one thinks expired records are no longer "delivered records" in the relevant sense. A criticism of the first: it lets a dead revision keep a live one buried forever, which may be undesirable operationally.

A third disagreement is what a criticism targets. One can criticize a reconstruction rule, a particular record, a booking's history, the snapshot as a whole, or the assumption that logical time is meaningful. For example, saying "this snapshot is inconsistent" might mean two active holds for one booking at the same greatest revision, or it might mean total reservations exceed capacity, or it might mean the logical time is behind an expiry that someone expected to have passed. These are different claims. A conjecture: many apparent disagreements about availability are really disagreements about which target a criticism addresses. A criticism of the rule "higher revision always supersedes" is not the same as a criticism of a record that carries a high revision but an implausible quantity. Preserving that distinction matters because one can reject a rule while accepting the data, or accept the rule while rejecting the data as corrupt or late.

A fourth disagreement concerns source assumptions. The snapshot assumes records are delivered, but not that they are complete. It assumes duplicates convey no additional authority, but not that all duplicates are identical in every field; if two records share booking and revision but differ in kind or quantity, are they duplicates or alternatives? The description says duplicate deliveries convey no additional authority, which suggests exact duplicates are inert, but near-duplicates may be unresolved alternatives. It assumes logical current time is a single coordinate, but different replicas may have different logical times; if so, expiry is replica-relative. It assumes bookings are independent, but capacity is shared, so reservations interact. It assumes a release or expired hold reserves zero, but does not say whether a release at a lower revision can cancel a hold at a higher revision. By the supersession rule, no: the higher hold wins. By a cancellation rule, maybe yes. That is a source assumption about what "release" means.

A fifth disagreement is whether availability should be computed per booking or globally. Per booking, one can say each booking's reservation is the quantity of its greatest-revision active hold, or zero otherwise, or unresolved among tied greatest-revision active holds. Globally, availability is capacity minus the sum. But if there are unresolved alternatives, the sum is not well-defined. One can compute a lower bound by taking the minimum reservation per booking and an upper bound by taking the maximum. That gives an interval, but intervals lose correlations: booking A's high alternative might be incompatible with booking B's high alternative if they share a physical resource not named in the snapshot. The snapshot does not name physical resources, so this incompatibility is invisible. A conjecture: the snapshot is under-specified for any real warehouse, and the best one can do is expose the unresolved alternatives rather than pretend to a single answer. A criticism: exposing alternatives without a policy for resolving them pushes the problem downstream, where it may be resolved badly or inconsistently.

A sixth disagreement concerns negative availability. If capacity is 10 and active holds sum to 12, availability is -2. Some might call this an inconsistency and reject the snapshot. Others might call it a valid state of over-reservation. The description says availability can be negative, which suggests over-reservation is allowed. The snapshot is not a single ledger. It is a cloud of rival stories about what has been promised. The capacity and logical time are shared coordinates—or viewpoints, depending on which replica you ask—but the records arrive as a bag. A higher revision supersedes a lower revision for that booking, within that booking. Two bookings can disagree about which revision they have accepted without infecting each other. ## Per-booking reconstruction and its residual conflicts

For any one booking, the natural grouping is by revision, keeping the greatest revision present. Within that greatest revision, a hold and a release are not both in force as the same fact; they are alternatives. An expired hold and a release both reserve zero. An active hold reserves its quantity. If several active holds tie at the greatest revision, they remain unresolved alternatives—not a sum, not a vote.

Globally, availability is capacity minus the sum. But if there are unresolved alternatives, the sum is not well-defined. **Sixth disagreement: negative availability.** If capacity is 10 and active holds sum to 12, availability is −2. Some might call this an inconsistency and reject the snapshot. **Eighth disagreement: tie-breaking across bookings.** Different bookings need not share the same choice, so one cannot impose a global tiebreak. **Ninth disagreement: time.** Logical current time is given, but records have expiries. If logical time advances, expired holds become zero. Does an expired hold at a high revision still supersede a lower active hold? One reading says yes; another says expiry is a state change that makes the high revision inactive, allowing a lower revision to become relevant if it is still active. The description does not resolve this. RSS: both are readings. The conjecture that the safer reading is that supersession is structural and expiry is evaluative—RSS carries it as a conjecture about a reading. The criticism that this can leave a booking with no reservation even though an older active hold exists, which may violate an operator's expectation—RSS carries it as a criticism of a reading, not as a refutation.

**Tenth disagreement: what "delivered" means.** A record delivered to one replica may not be delivered to another. The snapshot is described as replicated, but the bag is unordered. Does the snapshot represent the union of all deliveries, or the intersection, or one replica's view? If it is a union, it may contain alternatives that no single replica has. If it is an intersection, it may omit records that matter. RSS: a delivery is an event that makes a record available; deliveries are not ordered, may be repeated, and may differ in logical time if they come from different replicas. The bag is the raw material, not the story. RSS does not decide union, intersection, or single-view; it represents the snapshot as a merge of replica views, without deciding which. The conjecture that the snapshot is a merge, and merging is itself a source of uncertainty—RSS treats this as an account-level conjecture. The criticism that the description treats the snapshot as a single object, which may obscure the replication problem rather than solve it—RSS accepts this as a criticism of the primitive "viewpoint," which is what the snapshot is, not what it replaces.

## What remains material for inquiry

False or incomplete proposals are not discarded; they are part of the evidence about how people understand the system. A conjecture that a release always cancels a hold, even across revisions, may be false under the stated supersession rule, but it reveals an assumption about what releases are for. A conjecture that ties should be summed may be false under the "unresolved alternatives" reading, but it reveals a desire for conservatism. A criticism that the snapshot is unusable because it does not resolve ties may be substantive, but it may also be a demand for a decision that the snapshot was never meant to make.

Keeping these disagreements visible is not a failure of the reconstruction; it is the reconstruction's only honest form. In RSS, this is represented by inquiry states: a collection of accounts plus a set of open questions. Open questions are not solved by RSS; they are carried forward. A conjecture is open if no account has committed to it or refuted it. A commitment is an account's acceptance of a conjecture. A refutation is one of: a counterexample within an account's own viewpoint; a derivation of inconsistency within an account's own reading; or a demonstration that a conjecture depends on an assumption that another account rejects. Refutations are local to accounts and do not force global agreement.

## What RSS may obstruct

RSS may obstruct efficient decision-making because it refuses to produce a single answer. It may obstruct comparison between accounts because it lacks a common metric. It may obstruct automation because it is noncomputable and requires human or external choice. It may obstruct reasoning about physical resources because it does not include a resource model unless one is added as a primitive. It may obstruct reasoning about time across replicas because it treats logical time as viewpoint-relative without a mechanism for aligning viewpoints. It may obstruct the very idea of a snapshot as a single object, because it treats a snapshot as one viewpoint among many.

## Unresolved expressive limitations

RSS cannot express the exact provenance of a delivery unless provenance is added. RSS cannot express physical resource sharing beyond what an account includes. RSS cannot express replica agreement protocols. RSS cannot express the operational cost of retaining uncertainty. RSS cannot express the authority of a delivery beyond the record fields. RSS does not resolve the disagreements it represents, and it does not claim to. Ordinary prose remains available to criticize RSS for being too permissive, too vague, or too detached from operational needs.
